ms.report:
Powerpoint decks for the expert working groups
In preparation for the expert working groups, we developed the Speciality Tea Working Group powerpoint deck. The aim of these workshops as mentioned in the proposal is to ensure we get buy-in from the key industry experts in order to adopt the system. The full powerpoint deck can be found here: Expert Working Group Session Material.
In order to do this, we need to explain the 5S Tea Classification System as well as the blockchain tools that will be utilized to implement these systems. The agenda for these sessions are as follows:
・Global Speciality Tea Trends: to really cement the key themes and need for our systems
・Cambridge 5S Speciality Tea Categorisation System: deep-dive into how this works
・Ecosystem Governance and Cardano-based Tooling
・QnA and Working Group Discussions

Report on Global Speciality Tea Industry - ecosystem governance analysis and opportunities
The team has conducted an 18 page report providing a deep-dive into the global tea ecosystem and trends. The full report can be found here: Global Tea Ecosystem Report. The beginning of this report covers a number of overview topics such as the global tea market’s production, consumption and thematics. The report then covers a deep-dive into the Sri Lankan segment which has been a key focus area for this proposal. Finally, the capstone section is the ecosystem governance chapter which covers in detail how minimum viable governance can be implemented. There is a strong focus in this report on leveraging blockchain solutions and tooling available already on Cardano. 
Summarizing the key findings for the ecosystem governance chapter;
・Ecosystem Stakeholders: there are a number of key stakeholders in the tea sector. ms.report:
Summary of Milestone 4 requirement: Conduct 2 Physical Workshops

The zenGate Global team was accompanied by Joyce Maina between the 7th to 16th of December to conduct workshops as part of this proposal. The full report with the photos can be viewed here: Sri Lanka Workshop Summary.

Workshop 1
The first workshop was conducted on the 13th of December with key officials from the Sri Lankan Tea Board and expert tea tasters. The session involved an interactive tea-tasting workshop whilst applying the 5S System. This was critical to get buy-in from the regulators and experts on the ground. 

Workshop 2
The second workshop was conducted on the 14th of December, with nearly 100 people attending - from all over the Sri Lankan tea sector. This was held in the old Tea Auction room - where the physical auctions used to be sold, signiFrom regulators, producers, exports, brokers and traders. This session was a 2.5 hour workshop with a QnA session at the very end. The Chairman of the Tea Board also did a keynote presentation to open up the workshop. 

Other workshops conducted in Sri Lanka:
In the lead up to the workshops, the team did a number of on-site visits to tea gardens and primary producers. During these visits, they conducted smaller scale workshops going into detail how the 5S system works and how blockchain technology can be implemented to improve quality and traceability needs. 

General thoughts and takeaways from the workshops
・Initially thought the Tea Board might be hard to convince, but had overwhelming support from the inside - strong level of respect amongst the tea tasters. They have become strong advocates and the relationship building here was a super important takeaway. 

・Better clarity on the levels / depth of training required across various segments:
・Producers (need in-person training)
・Regulator
・Quality grader / taster
・Buyer (wholesale)
・Consumer

PoA Resubmission Notes: April 5th
This is a re-submission of the PoA, addressing comments made from a non-approval on the 3rd of April by one of the reviewers who were asking whether we can upload videos of the working groups. I spoke with a reviewer of the Atala Telegram and have been given some advice on how to move forward as there are some reasons behind why we have not done this. 
We want to make it clear that videos are not part of the required evidence and that the required evidence has already been submitted. If there were questions around this, it should have been raised at the very beginning of the project when the Milestones were drafted and approved - we could have clearly defined our reasoning behind this at that point of time to avoid any confusion now.
We also want to make it clear, whilst our own team's outputs are open-source, but that the leading outside experts whose inputs are required are not part of the team and are not bound by the open source aspect. Outside commodity/tea market experts have their own privacy concerns and are not as forthcoming if every word is being publicly recorded and broadcast. 
Hope this explains our decision behind not publishing videos or a full transcript. We will continue to be as transparent as possible and have done so with the submission below.
